about: Hand-made answer key for the MCP front door (data/POLICY.md section 7).

It was written from the policy and from the MCP specification, NOT by running src/mcp_server.py. It says what the server must answer. tests/test_mcp.py plays every case against the server and compares.
A case sends messages (one per line) and lists what must come back. 'send' and 'expect' line up one to one. null in 'expect' means: the server must write NOTHING for that message.

Send shortcuts: {'raw': text} sends that text as the line. {'raw_hex': hex} sends those bytes. {'raw_repeat': [text, n]} sends text repeated n times. {'raw_nested': n} sends n opening and n closing square brackets.
{'ask': question, 'id': n} is a tools/call of ask_documents with that question. {'ask_args': {...}, 'id': n} is the same with these exact arguments.

Inside any message, {'@meta': 'modern'} becomes the standard metadata of a 2026-07-28 request, and {'@repeat': [text, n]} becomes text repeated n times. {'@chars': [numbers]} becomes the text made of those Unicode code points, so that this file stays plain ASCII.
Expect shortcuts: {'id': n, 'tool': {'text': t, 'isError': b}} is a tool result with exactly one text item.

Matching: an object matches if every listed key matches (extra keys are allowed), a list must have the same length, '@any' = any non-empty text, '@absent' = the key must not exist, {'@length': n} = text, list or object of that length, {'@exact': x} = equal with no extra keys anywhere.

Other case fields: 'token' names the sign-in token in the server's environment (premkumar, dhanesh, nobody, none, empty, garbage, expired, future, wrong_key, alg_none, changed_payload, long_life; default none). 'handshake': 'legacy' first sends initialize and the initialized notification.
'calls' lists what the outside world was asked, in order. 'audit' lists the log lines the front door itself must write. 'fail' makes one outside call raise an error. 'no_key' removes the signing key.
